h: From Engineer's Legacy to Museum of the Year
p: The gallery was founded in 1889 in memory of Sir Joseph Whitworth, the Manchester engineer famous for his precision machine tools and his standard screw thread. It became part of the University of Manchester in 1958, and the 2015 redevelopment, which added glass-walled wings reaching out into the park, gave it a whole new lease of life. You can see the Victorian origins and the modern additions sitting side by side as you walk through.

Look out for the art garden and the landscape-inspired gallery that brings the outside in. Watching the trees through the huge windows while you look at art is part of the experience. Entry to the gallery is free, with donations welcome, so you can drop in for half an hour or settle in for longer.
Allow around one to two hours. Buses run up and down Oxford Road constantly, so it's easy to reach from Piccadilly and the city centre without a car.

Just up the road, Manchester Museum is another free university museum and well worth pairing with the Whitworth. It has natural history, ancient Egypt and a cast of a Tyrannosaurus rex that kids love. When you're hungry, Wilmslow Road through Rusholme, known as the Curry Mile, is only a few minutes south, with restaurants, sweet shops and late-opening dessert spots lining the street. It's a brilliant way to finish a day of culture with a proper Manchester feed.
